newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Seagate opens Singapore hard disk plants.
newsitem.headline: Seagate opens Singapore hard disk plants.

text.p: U.S. electronics company Seagate Technology Inc opened two giant new computer disk plants in Singapore on Tuesday, further strengthening the city-state's dominance in the production of computer data storage.
Company officials said the two plants, which will employ 900 staff, represented a total investment of around US$200 million.

The plants would have a combined annual production capacity of up to 50 million of the 3.5-inch circular aluminium coated hard disks -- also known as disk media -- equivalent to around half the company's total worldwide disk output.
Seagate is the world's biggest independent manufacturer of hard disk drives and related components with around a third of the market and already makes about 18 percent of the world's disk media.
William Watkins, the chief operating officer for Seagate's recording media group, said Singapore was an increasingly important centre for the company's operations.
"Singapore is the centre of our media operation. Seagate is very committed to Singapore and we have several plants here," Watkins told Reuters in an interview.
"When we get up to full production, about 50 percent of our media disk production will come from here," he added.

Opening the new plants, Trade and Industry Minister Yeo Cheow Tong said his department aimed to strengthen Singapore's dominance in the electronics industry further over the next few years through the introduction of new companies.

Singapore is already a major centre for computer and computer-related products and produces around 45 percent of the world's hard disk-drives. Electronics and related products account for almost half its industrial output and around 60 percent of non-oil exports.
"By the year 2000, we hope to produce as much as 30 percent of the world's hard disk media here to support this important industry cluster," Yeo said.
The new plants bring Seagate's total investment in Singapore to more than Singapore $1.2 billion (US$851 million).
Watkins said Seagate had chosen Singapore for the new plants because of the high quality of the local workforce.

"Both these facilities represent state of the art process manufacturing for which we need highly trained people," he said. "We spent a lot of our capital training and the labour force here is outstanding."
He said Seagate was taking the current downturn in the worldwide electronics industry in its stride and expected the market to improve again.
"We have made some adjustments here in what we are doing as we upgrade our drives to higher storage. But I'm actually quite positive looking forward. We're very much on a growth pattern," he said.
Yeo said the Seagate investment was "a sign of confidence in our collective ability to ride out the temporary slowdown in the global electronics industry".
"The current slowdown is cyclical. Seagate has rightly take the longer-term view," he said.
